Triage notes (quick):
- Observed: queue depth on CrestPay-dedicated-us-east jumped from baseline ~120 to ~1,850 concurrent requests between 08:40–09:05 ET.
- Impact: p95 latency increased from ~480ms to ~2.8s; 5xx rate rose to 3.7% (mostly 504/502 downstream timeouts).
- Root cause signals: noisy high-throughput job from a downstream integration + slower KV cache hit rate (eviction storm) amplified tail-latency.

Immediate recommendations (can act now):
1) Failover a fraction of hot traffic to a hosted-compatible variant (model: open-gglm-7b-quant) with identical interface but lower latency profile. This requires a config toggle (can be done in 10m) and will reduce load on the dedicated pool.
2) Temporarily throttle the client’s high-concurrency routes (rate-limit key) as a protective QOS (needs customer sign-off).
3) Request emergency burst capacity allocation on the Dedicated cluster (+20% headroom) — needs exec authorization and procurement sign-off for the associated charge.

I’ve attached a CSV snapshot of queue metrics for the last 90 minutes.

[attachment: queue-snapshot-20270914.csv]

If we do (1) + (2) now we should see queue reduction within 8–12 minutes and p95 back below 700ms. If you want me to flip the hosted fallback I’ll queue it and notify once done.

— David
